Data Model Description: Creates shared framework routines and core reference tables used across JCT modules and extensions.

Canonical ADP Workforce Now model built from the ADP REST API tables that Apps/ADP.py loads: worker demographics, HR Workers v2 (optional), the cost center, department and job validation tables, and per-worker time cards with day entries. CommonWSDataset flattens each response into _MDD_SR_ADP_ tables; ADP.py stamps the join keys CommonWSDataset cannot keep (assignmentItemID, entryItemID, listItemCode, timeCardID and per-entry keys). _MDD_JCT_ADP.SQL builds employees scoped to the primary work assignment, org units, addresses, phones, email, ethnicity, race, jobs, departments, cost centers, locations, supervisory relationships, pay periods, time cards, daily and period totals, time punches, labor allocations, earning codes and row level security. A collection without the newer keys or optional sources still builds, with each affected join falling back to a deterministic pick.
Builds the current set of custom JCT Alerts email events and current SQL validation findings using Trigger ID as the sole durable event identity.

Canonical CSS SurveyMonkey model and PnP dashboard outputs built from SR_CSS shared tables.
Canonical JCT model for Microsoft Entra ID users, groups, sign-ins, authentication methods, MFA reporting, tenant information, and report-facing unpivot outputs.

This is a data model designed to make it easy to interact with data from the NextGen Enterprise (NGE) EHR. It reads the NextGen tables in place and builds JCT tables with the same names and meanings as JCT for Credible wherever NextGen has the data.

Canonical Paycom model built from the Paycom REST API tables that Apps/Paycom.py loads. CommonWSDataset flattens each endpoint response into _MDD_SR_PAYCOM_ tables, and _MDD_JCT_PAYCOM.SQL builds employees (with dates, age and tenure groups, email, position and up to four supervisors), cost centers, addresses, phones and email in the PaycomPR shape, supervisory relationships and row level security in the Rippling shape, time punches, punch labor allocation segments and the punch audit trail, plus precedent entities for positions, position levels, position seats, locations, establishments, labor allocations, earning codes and new hires. Payments and pay periods have no API route, so PaycomPR remains the source for those.

Appointment reminder send queue, recipients, settings and Twilio send history, built from EHR-neutral custom tables the agency specifics fill. Apps/Reminders.py sends from the queue.

Canonical Rippling Payroll / HRIS model built from normalized Rippling REST API shared-resource tables. Source API JSON is recursively normalized by CommonWSDataset into SR parent/child tables, then _MDD_JCT_RIPPLING.SQL composes employees, organization structures, contact media, pay periods, time punches, segments, supervisory relationships, and RLS support outputs. Field semantics use SQL/code and the supplied SR discovery pack as structural evidence, with official Rippling REST API documentation used for source-field meaning where available.
Produces CCBHC UMD service-level output for Credible with agency and proxy identifiers.

Builds the narrow tables the Credible Client Population plug and play report reads: one row per client attribute for the report's drop-downs (client fields, client extended fields and current diagnoses) and one row per service within the agency's lookback.

Data model for Mission Driven Data's integration between Credible and Eleos, preserving Eleos-requested field mappings, source references, and export semantics. Every table except the settings tables carries two flags, [Eleos Eligible Initial] and [Eleos Eligible Rolling], set to 1 or 0. Eleos takes two windows: an initial send of the last 180 days when an agency starts, and a rolling daily feed of the last 30 days after that. Each flag says whether the row belongs in that window, so Apps/Eleos.py only filters on a flag (--compliance-feed-initial reads the Initial flag, --compliance-feed the Rolling flag) and every file it sends agrees on what is in scope. The windows are set in the SETTINGS table (lookback_days_initial, lookback_days_rolling). The tables themselves hold more history than either window, lookback_days (365 by default).
